title: Migration Matrix — S130 Duplicated Paths → S131 computeEvidenceGraph()

duplicatedPaths.s130Finding: scan session history for attempts — 12 independent implementations scanning data.sessions[].attempts, topicPerformance aggregates, casePatterns, or per-session mcqs
duplicatedPaths.targetEvidenceGraphField: computeEvidenceGraph() calls getTopicProgress(), getTrends(), getWeaknessClusters() internally — all session scanning is consolidated into a single pre-computation pipeline. Subsystems consume evidence[topic].totalAttempts, evidence[topic].correctCount, and metadata.sessionCount instead of scanning sessions independently.
duplicatedPaths.migrationDetail: Each subsystem replaces its independent sessions.slice(-N).attempts scan with a read from computeEvidenceGraph().evidence[topic].totalAttempts or computeEvidenceGraph().metadata.sessionCount. The 7-session-weekly-window use case is handled by getEvidenceWindows() which partitions the graph by recency.

duplicatedPaths.s130Finding: per-topic accuracy computation — 7 implementations computing accuracy from v.c / v.n * 100, 4 independent and 3 delegated to getTopicProgress()
duplicatedPaths.targetEvidenceGraphField: evidence[topic].accuracy (overall), evidence[topic].recentAccuracy (last 5 attempts), evidence[topic].timeWeightedAccuracy (EWMA 14-day half-life). All three are pre-computed by computeEvidenceGraph() from a single call to getTopicProgress() + _computeTimeWeightedAccuracy().
duplicatedPaths.migrationDetail: All 7 implementations replace their local Math.round(v.c/v.n*100) with evidence[topic].accuracy, evidence[topic].recentAccuracy, or evidence[topic].timeWeightedAccuracy depending on the desired time horizon. S127/S128 weekly scans use getEvidenceWindows().recent[topic].accuracy for week-scoped data.

duplicatedPaths.s130Finding: classify topic as weak (below threshold) — 8 implementations using 4 different threshold combinations: >=5/<60%, >=3/<60%, per-session <60%, <65% recommended focus
currentImplementations: May._identifyLearningPatterns() S124 ~1268 (>=5 attempts, <60% — delegates to getTopicProgress)
May._suggestFocusAreas() S125 ~1396 (>=5 attempts, <60% — delegates to getTopicProgress)
May._suggestFocusAreas() S125 ~1406 (calculation-miss conditional on current answer)
duplicatedPaths.targetEvidenceGraphField: observations.weaknesses[] — unified at >=5 attempts AND accuracy <60% in _deriveObservations() line 1564. Each entry carries topic, accuracy, recentAccuracy, timeWeightedAccuracy, totalAttempts, and evidence sub-object.
duplicatedPaths.migrationDetail: S127/S128 must change from their independent 7-session >=3/<60% scan to consuming observations.weaknesses (>=5/<60% lifetime). For weekly-digest 'Topics needing attention' that legitimately needs a shorter window, use getEvidenceWindows().recent and filter those with accuracy<60 (without the separate >=3 threshold — recency window provides the lookback). S126's per-session weak (any n>0, <60%) is a different concept (session-level weakness) and should remain per-session but should NOT be conflated with topic-level weakness — use a distinct label like 'struggled_this_session'.

duplicatedPaths.s130Finding: classify topic as strong (above threshold) — 6 implementations using 3 different threshold combinations: >=85%, >=70%, top-2 by session pct
currentImplementations: May._identifyLearningPatterns() S124 ~1259 (>=3 attempts, >=85% — delegates to getTopicProgress)
May._suggestFocusAreas() S125 ~1445 (>=3 attempts, >=85% — delegates to getTopicProgress)
May._generateWeeklyDigest() S127 ~3113 (>=3 attempts, >=70% — INDEPENDENT weekly scan)
May._generateStudyStrategy() S128 ~3256 (>=3 attempts, >=70% — INDEPENDENT weekly scan)
May._generateSessionRecap() S126 ~2965 (top-2 by pct, any n>0 — INDEPENDENT)
duplicatedPaths.targetEvidenceGraphField: observations.strengths[] — unified at >=3 attempts AND accuracy >=85 AND direction NOT declining/slightly_declining in _deriveObservations() line 1554. Each entry carries topic, accuracy, recentAccuracy, timeWeightedAccuracy, totalAttempts, stability, and evidence sub-object.
duplicatedPaths.migrationDetail: S127/S128's >=70% threshold creates a 'strong' label for topics that are moderate by the unified >=85% standard. The S130 canonical source proposal recommends adding a 'solid' tier (>=70%) to getTopicStrengthTiers(). Until that is built into computeEvidenceGraph(), S127/S128 should consume observations.strengths at >=85% and separately identify 'solid' topics (>=70%, <85%) from evidence[topic].accuracy if a secondary tier is needed. S126's top-2 strongest-areas is session-level and should remain separate but labeled distinctly.

duplicatedPaths.s130Finding: detect improvement trend — 7 implementations using 4 different delta thresholds: 15%, 10%, 10%, 5%
currentImplementations: MayLearnerState.classifyPendingOutcomes() S129 ~1270 (delta >= 5% AND accuracy >= 60% AND direction improving)
duplicatedPaths.targetEvidenceGraphField: observations.topicTrends[] — unified at >=4 attempts AND delta >= 10 in _deriveObservations() line 1573-1574. Also evidence[topic].direction (from getTrends with >=15% for 'improving', >5% for 'slightly_improving'). computeEvidenceGraph() layers both: getTrends provides fine-grained direction, _deriveObservations adds the >=10 delta gate for topicTrends observations.
duplicatedPaths.migrationDetail: This is the most complex migration because getTrends() itself uses delta>=15% for 'improving' while _deriveObservations (S131) uses delta>=10 for topicTrends. S124/S125's additional recentPct>=75% condition is dropped in the unified model. S129 classifyPendingOutcomes already delegates to getTrends().direction (indirectly through trendMap), so its delta>=5 gate becomes: check evidence[topic].direction for 'improving'/'slightly_improving' (from getTrends delta>5%) AND evidence[topic].delta>=10. S126/S127 session-comparison trends are a different concept and should remain but use consistent thresholds — or better, call getTrends() with the relevant data window.

duplicatedPaths.s130Finding: misconception pattern name lookup — identical pattern-name mapping object duplicated 7 times across may-core.js
duplicatedPaths.targetEvidenceGraphField: observations.misconceptions[] — unified misconception aggregation in _deriveObservations() line 1592-1598. However note: S131 _deriveObservations pushes RAW pattern keys (e.g. 'variance_sign_confusion'), not human-readable labels. The pattern-name lookup duplication still exists at S131 — a separate getMisconceptionLabels() canonical function is still needed (proposed in S130 §canonicalSourceProposal.misconceptions).
duplicatedPaths.migrationDetail: Step 1: create MayLearnerState.getMisconceptionLabels() returning the single canonical pattern→label mapping. Step 2: replace all 7 inline patternNames objects with calls to getMisconceptionLabels(). Step 3: _deriveObservations() can optionally include labels in observations.misconceptions[] entries. This is low-effort but not yet implemented in S131 — the observations are unified but the label lookup is still duplicated.

duplicatedPaths.s130Finding: recommend next study action — 6 independent recommendation functions using different data windows, thresholds (60% vs 65%), and priority rules (persistentWeak vs declining vs session-weakest)
currentImplementations: May._generateSessionRecap() S126 ~3041 (uses weakest topic from session)
May._generateWeeklyDigest() S127 ~3174 (uses weekly weak topics + patterns, <65% threshold)
May._generateStudyStrategy() S128 ~3266 (uses weekly weak/strong topics, <60% threshold)
duplicatedPaths.targetEvidenceGraphField: computeEvidenceGraph() provides evidence, observations, and clusters but does NOT yet include a unified getRecommendedActions() function. The S130 canonical source proposal recommends MayLearnerState.getRecommendedActions({ horizon }) as a new function consuming computeEvidenceGraph() output. Currently no direct target field exists.
duplicatedPaths.migrationDetail: Requires building a new MayLearnerState.getRecommendedActions({ horizon: 'session'|'week'|'2weeks' }) that consumes computeEvidenceGraph() output (observations.weaknesses, clusters.persistentWeak, clusters.declining, observations.misconceptions) and returns a ranked action list with consistent prioritization rules: (1) persistent weak topics, (2) declining topics, (3) misconception-heavy topics, (4) unstable topics. All 6 current implementations then delegate to this single function with their horizon parameter.

classificationConflicts.s130Conflict: S124/S125/getWeaknessClusters() use >=5 attempts/<60% (all-history). S127/S128 use >=3 attempts/<60% (7-day window). S127 also has a separate <65% 'recommended focus' threshold. A topic with 4 attempts at 55% this week is flagged weak by S127/S128 but NOT by S124/S125/getWeaknessClusters().
classificationConflicts.s131Resolution: _deriveObservations() line 1564 unifies on >=5 attempts AND accuracy <60%. All subsystems consume observations.weaknesses[] for topic-level weakness classification. The 7-day window concern is handled via getEvidenceWindows().recent — subsystems filter observations by recency instead of re-scanning data with different attempt thresholds.

classificationConflicts.s130Conflict: S124/S125 use >=3 attempts/>=85%. S127/S128 use >=3 attempts/>=70%. A topic at 75% with 4 attempts is strong per S127/S128 but not per S124/S125.
classificationConflicts.s131Resolution: _deriveObservations() line 1554 unifies on >=3 attempts AND accuracy >=85 AND direction not declining/slightly_declining. The >=70% tier from S127/S128 can be recovered by reading evidence[topic].accuracy directly for a 'solid' label, or by adding a solidTopic tier to getTopicStrengthTiers() as recommended by S130. All subsystems consume observations.strengths[] for the canonical 'strong' label.

classificationConflicts.s130Conflict: getTrends() uses delta>=15% for 'improving'. S124/S125 use delta>=10% AND recentPct>=75%. S126 uses session-to-session delta>=10%. S127 uses first-vs-last delta>=10%. S129 uses delta>=5% AND accuracy>=60%. Multiple conflicting signals across subsystems for the same topic.
classificationConflicts.s131Resolution: _deriveObservations() line 1573 unifies on >=4 attempts AND delta >= 10 for observations.topicTrends[].improving. getTrends() still provides fine-grained direction (improving at >=15%, slightly_improving at >5%) in evidence[topic].direction which remains available for subsystems that need more granularity. The two thresholds coexist in a layered model: direction from getTrends (fine-grained), binary improving/declining gate from _deriveObservations (>=10 delta, >=4 attempts). S129 classifyPendingOutcomes already delegates to getTrends().direction and can use evidence[topic].direction from computeEvidenceGraph().

classificationConflicts.s130Conflict: getTrends() uses delta<=-15% for 'declining'. S126 uses session-to-session delta<=-10%. S127 uses first-vs-last delta<=-10%. A topic with delta=-12% is declining per S126/S127 but only 'slightly_declining' per getTrends().
classificationConflicts.s131Resolution: _deriveObservations() line 1580 unifies on >=4 attempts AND delta <= -10 for observations.topicTrends[].declining. The layered model (getTrends direction for granularity + _deriveObservations gate for binary classification) applies symmetrically to declining.

classificationConflicts.s130Conflict: All 5 subsystems read from the same data.misconceptionPatterns source and filter by count>=2, so they CANNOT disagree on which misconceptions exist. However the pattern-names mapping is duplicated in 7 locations creating maintenance risk — a new pattern must be added to 7 separate inline objects.
classificationConflicts.s131Resolution: observations.misconceptions[] in _deriveObservations() centralizes the 'count >= 2' filter and misconception aggregation into one place. However the human-readable pattern name mapping is NOT yet centralized — _deriveObservations stores raw pattern keys. The S130 proposal for a getMisconceptionLabels() canonical function has not yet been implemented in S131. Partially resolved: aggregation unified, label lookup still duplicated.

classificationConflicts.s130Conflict: S125 prioritizes based on getTopicProgress() (all history, <60%). S127 recommends from weekly scan with <65% threshold. S128 prioritizes from weekly scan with <60% threshold. A topic at 63% with 6 attempts this week would be recommended by S127 (<65%) but NOT by S125 or S128 (<60%).
classificationConflicts.s131Resolution: computeEvidenceGraph() provides observations.weaknesses[] (unified at <60%) as the canonical weak-topic list. However coarser-grained topic prioritization with different thresholds (like S127's <65% 'recommended focus') is a recommendation-layer concern that computeEvidenceGraph() does not directly address. Resolved for the weak/not-weak binary classification, but the recommendation ranking with variable thresholds still needs the getRecommendedActions() function. Partially resolved.

classificationConflicts.s130Conflict: S126 compares most-recent session to immediately-prior session. S127 compares first to last session within the 7-session window. Different baselines produce different delta magnitudes and sometimes different directions.
classificationConflicts.s131Resolution: computeEvidenceGraph() uses getTrends() which computes delta as recentPct - accuracy (recent 5 vs overall), a topic-level trend metric, not session-to-session comparison. The S126/S127 session-comparison trends are a different concept (session-over-session performance vs topic trend). S131 resolves the conflict by providing evidence[topic].delta and evidence[topic].direction as the single source for topic trend. Session-to-session comparisons, if still needed, should use a separate, explicitly-labeled sessionDelta field — neither S126 nor S127 should call their session comparisons 'improving'/'declining' as those labels now belong to topic-level trends from getTrends().

directReplacements_detail: 1. Scan session history (12→1): subsystems read evidence[topic].totalAttempts and metadata.sessionCount instead of scanning sessions independently
2. Per-topic accuracy (7→1): subsystems read evidence[topic].accuracy, .recentAccuracy, or .timeWeightedAccuracy instead of computing v.c/v.n*100 locally
3. Misconception labels (7→1): requires creating getMisconceptionLabels() — counted here because the 7 copies are replaced by 1 canonical function call (low-effort restructure)
thresholdAdaptations_detail: 1. Weak classification (8→1): S127/S128 adapt from >=3/<60% weekly to consuming observations.weaknesses (>=5/<60% lifetime); S126 relabeled as session-level
2. Strong classification (6→1): S127/S128 adapt from >=70% to consuming observations.strengths (>=85%); optional 'solid' tier (>=70%) from evidence[topic].accuracy
3. Improvement trend (7→1): all subsystems adapt from varying delta thresholds (15/10/10/5) to observations.topicTrends (delta>=10) with evidence[topic].direction for fine-grained needs
restructuresNeeded_detail: 1. Recommendations (6→1): requires building getRecommendedActions({horizon}) as a new function consuming computeEvidenceGraph(); all 6 recommendation paths delegate to it
2. Misconception labels (7→1): requires creating getMisconceptionLabels() and replacing 7 inline patternName maps; observations are unified but labels are not yet (partial S131 coverage)
alreadyResolvedByS131_detail: cross_session_trend_comparison: getTrends() provides single delta/direction for topic-level trends; session-level comparisons use distinct labeling

strong.threshold: totalAttempts >= 3 AND accuracy >= 85 AND direction NOT declining/slightly_declining

improving.threshold: totalAttempts >= 4 AND delta !== null AND delta >= 10

declining.threshold: totalAttempts >= 4 AND delta !== null AND delta <= -10

s131ThresholdVerification.note: getTrends() internal thresholds differ (>=15% for 'improving', <=-15% for 'declining', >5% for 'slightly_improving', <-5% for 'slightly_declining') and feed evidence[topic].direction. _deriveObservations applies a second gate at delta>=10 / delta<=-10 for binary topicTrends observations. This layered design provides both fine-grained direction and binary classification.

gapsInS131Coverage.impact: 7 inline pattern-name map objects still duplicated across may-core.js
gapsInS131Coverage.s130Recommendation: Create MayLearnerState.getMisconceptionLabels() returning the single canonical mapping; _deriveObservations can optionally include labels in observations.misconceptions[] entries

gapsInS131Coverage.impact: 6 independent recommendation functions still produce conflicting next-study-action advice
gapsInS131Coverage.s130Recommendation: Build MayLearnerState.getRecommendedActions({ horizon }) consuming computeEvidenceGraph() output with consistent prioritization: persistentWeak > declining > misconception-heavy > unstable

gapsInS131Coverage.impact: S127/S128's >=70% 'strong' label has no equivalent in computeEvidenceGraph(); subsystems needing this tier must compute it from evidence[topic].accuracy independently
gapsInS131Coverage.s130Recommendation: Add solidTopic tier to observations or extend evidence[topic] with a strengthTier field (strong/solid/developing/weak)
